title: Finding 3-Digit Even Numbers
summary: Given an array of digits, find all unique three-digit even numbers formed by any combination of the digits, ensuring no leading zeros, and return them in sorted order.
statement: Given an array of digits, find all unique three-digit even numbers formed by any combination of the digits, ensuring no leading zeros, and return them in sorted order.
constraints: digits contains at least three decimal digits and occurrences may repeat.
Use three distinct input positions to form a number from 100 through 999 whose last digit is even.
Return all unique qualifying numbers in increasing order.
hints: Enumerating the 450 three-digit even values automatically guarantees uniqueness and sorted order.
For each even value, compare its digit frequency map with the available input counts.
Accept value when needed[d]<=available[d] for every digit.
The count condition is necessary and sufficient to select distinct positions matching exactly the candidate digits.
editorial: The count condition is necessary and sufficient to select distinct positions matching exactly the candidate digits.

tests.explanation: The ten constructible even values are 102,120,130,132,210,230,302,310,312,320.
